# GIS Map Online

> GISMap.online is a free, open-source, browser-based GIS workspace for people and AI agents to explore, style and share geographic data in 2D and 3D. A language model can make a map for someone by producing a URL: no API key, account or server call is needed. It opens public ArcGIS REST (FeatureServer, MapServer, ImageServer), GeoJSON, WMS, WFS and KML sources over HTTPS.

The map in a link is one JSON object (map-v1): layers with filters and styles, basemap, camera. Write it after #map=json: in the URL. Invalid parts are skipped and reported; the rest of the map still opens.

## Links a chatbot can write (no code, no account)

Every GISMap artifact can be written as one link: URI-encode the JSON (encodeURIComponent) after `json:`. Return the link to the user; it opens the finished result.

- Map: `https://gismap.online/#map=json:{"version":1,"layers":[{"url":"<layer URL>","where":"<filter>","renderer":{"type":"choropleth","field":"<FIELD>","ramp":"purples"}}],"basemap":"gray-vector"}`
- Briefing (slides): add `"briefing":{"layerId":"<layer URL>","selection":{"useAll":true},"slides":[{"template":"title","title":"…"},{"template":"key-numbers","title":"At a glance","blocks":[{"type":"stat","stat":"count","label":"Features"}]},{"template":"feature","title":"…","featureId":"<OBJECTID>","fit":"feature","blocks":[{"type":"text","markdown":"…"}]}]}` to the map JSON; the link opens presenting (schema: [briefing-v1](https://gismap.online/schemas/briefing-v1.schema.json)).
- Guided tour: `https://gismap.online/?tourOnly=1#tour=json:{"title":"…","autoplay":true,"stops":[{"name":"Coit Tower","caption":"…","lat":37.80238,"lon":-122.40583,"zoom":17,"tilt":55,"heading":200,"basemap":"usgs-imagery","seconds":6}]}`
- LiDAR or 3D model (MapLibre engine): a map layer with `"type":"pointcloud"` (LAS, LAZ, XYZ) or `"type":"model"` (glTF/GLB, OBJ, PLY) and `"scene3d":{"crs":"EPSG:26910","classes":[3,4,5,14],"colorBy":"classification"}` or, for models, `"scene3d":{"anchor":[lon,lat,0],"heading":0,"scale":1}`.
- Field task: `https://gismap.online/?workflow=tasks#fieldTask=json:{"title":"…","location":"…","lat":37.75972,"lon":-122.42713,"notes":"…","steps":["…","…"]}` (up to 10 steps and 5 features: `{"layerUrl","objectId","lat","lon","label"}`).

Readable links hold up to 8,192 characters. Inspect real fields first (`<layer URL>?f=pjson`) and never invent coordinates. Use `usgs-imagery` for aerial imagery on the default MapLibre engine. Step-by-step: [agent recipes](https://gismap.online/agent-recipes/).

## What can AI agents create with GISMap?

Finished maps, briefings, guided tours, field task packages, 3D maps and themed maps. Start with [Discover](https://gismap.online/discover/) and its [current examples](https://gismap.online/discover/examples/) when choosing a public workflow. Each recipe gives the interface to use (a URL you write, a standalone JavaScript module, or the in-page API; never a hosted REST endpoint), how to verify the result, and its limits: [recipe pages](https://gismap.online/agent-recipes/) · [recipe catalog (JSON)](https://gismap.online/api/agent-recipes/index.json). For engine-specific work, read the [Map engines guide](https://gismap.online/discover/engines/) before selecting styling or 3D behavior.


| User asks for… | Agent selects… | Primary artifact |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Map this data and color it by population | [interactive-map](https://gismap.online/skills/#recipe-interactive-map) | Filtered, styled interactive map |
| Create slides about these districts | [interactive-briefing](https://gismap.online/skills/#recipe-interactive-briefing) | Map-based briefing |
| Show me these locations in sequence | [geographic-tour](https://gismap.online/skills/#recipe-geographic-tour) | Guided geographic tour |
| Inspect this location and complete these tasks | [field-tasks](https://gismap.online/skills/#recipe-field-tasks) | Five-task fieldwork package |
| Make the county heights represent acreage | [3d-extrusion](https://gismap.online/skills/#recipe-3d-extrusion) | 3D extruded map |
| Separate overlapping events by year and height | [spatial-3d-chart](https://gismap.online/skills/#recipe-spatial-3d-chart) | 3D spatial chart and five-scene Brief |
| Show this LiDAR or CAD model in 3D | [lidar-and-3d-models](https://gismap.online/skills/#recipe-lidar-and-3d-models) | Point cloud or 3D model map |
| Make the map feel like Halloween in California | [vibe-map](https://gismap.online/skills/#recipe-vibe-map) | Coordinated theme and styled map |

Combine recipes for one request: a 3D fire-history map with chronological strata, a five-slide briefing and a QR uses interactive-map, spatial-3d-chart and interactive-briefing. Check compatibility, virtual-Z semantics, actual outputs and reopening; do not assume every combination is portable.

## Make a map from a URL (no code)
- One layer: `https://gismap.online/?layer=<HTTPS service URL>&layerType=feature`
- Styled: add `&style=choropleth&field=<FIELD>&method=auto&ramp=greens&exclude=-1&basemap=gray-vector` (`method=auto` picks the class breaks from the data)
- Not sure which style suits the field: `&style=auto&field=<FIELD>` lets the app choose
- Full control: `https://gismap.online/#map=json:<URI-encoded map-v1 JSON>` (at most 8192 characters) or `?spec=<URL of a hosted map-v1 JSON file>`
- Inspect a service's fields first: append `?f=pjson` to the layer URL.
- Worked example: https://gismap.online/#map=json:%7B%22version%22%3A1%2C%22basemap%22%3A%22gray-vector%22%2C%22layers%22%3A%5B%7B%22url%22%3A%22https%3A%2F%2Fservices.arcgis.com%2FP3ePLMYs2RVChkJx%2FArcGIS%2Frest%2Fservices%2FCorn%2FFeatureServer%2F0%22%2C%22renderer%22%3A%7B%22type%22%3A%22choropleth%22%2C%22field%22%3A%22CORN_SALES_IN_DOLLARS%22%2C%22method%22%3A%22auto%22%2C%22ramp%22%3A%22greens%22%2C%22exclude%22%3A%5B-1%5D%7D%7D%5D%7D

## Finish and verify the map
1. Retrieve source metadata (append ?f=pjson), inspect actual fields and query real filter values; do not guess field names. Check the publisher's null and sentinel conventions.
2. Construct a map-v1 spec and validate it and its renderer. In code, mapSpec.prepareVerification(spec) returns a URL and an offline report; metadata, filtering, rendering and reopening remain not_checked until independently tested.
3. Generate the canonical URL using mapSpec.createLink or URI-encoded #map=json: JSON. Return the actual URL to the user.
4. With browser access, open it, wait for layers, check issues and verify the intended features, filter, style and camera. Reopen the share URL and check again. State explicitly what you could not check.
5. Use precise status: prepared (constructed), validated (validator accepted, review warnings), loaded (layers loaded), verified (intended map and reopened link confirmed). A plausible URL alone is not verified. See the agent guide for tested filters and a Michigan county example.

Follow-up refinement: [derive year and acreage maps from one filtered California fire map](https://gismap.online/examples/ai/california-fire-refinement/). Preserve the source, filter, basemap and camera; use map-v1 when a simple URL is insufficient. The linked example reports which checks remain unverified.

## Contracts
- [Map spec schema](https://gismap.online/schemas/map-v1.schema.json): layers, renderers, filters, camera, basemap
- [Renderer schema](https://gismap.online/schemas/renderer-v1.schema.json): choropleth, graduated symbols, categories, heat map, simple
- [Briefing schema](https://gismap.online/schemas/briefing-v1.schema.json): slides that present a map
- [Layer style schema](https://gismap.online/schemas/layer-style-v1.schema.json): a reusable 2D or 3D layer file from the Cartography Lab (colour, 3D height, filter, opacity); `gisMapOnline.layerStyles` saves, applies and turns it into a map link or briefing
- [Agent recipe schema](https://gismap.online/schemas/agent-recipe-v1.schema.json): the format of /api/agent-recipes/*.json
- Tours and field tasks without the app: `createEmbeddedTourUrl` from [tour-share.js](https://gismap.online/js/tour-share.js) and `createFieldTaskUrl` from [field-task-share.js](https://gismap.online/js/field-task-share.js) build their links (see the [tour](https://gismap.online/agent-recipes/geographic-tour/) and [field task](https://gismap.online/agent-recipes/field-tasks/) recipes)
- [URL parameters](https://gismap.online/api/url-parameters.json): every query and fragment parameter
- [Capabilities](https://gismap.online/api/capabilities.json): in-page API, tools, error codes, limits
- [Application manifest](https://gismap.online/api/manifest.json) and [API explorer](https://gismap.online/api/explorer/): privacy-safe state and live registry discovery
- [TypeScript types](https://gismap.online/js/gismap-core.d.ts)

## Guides
- [GISMap Agent Skill](https://gismap.online/skills/): installable instructions, validation and implementation proposal
- [Making maps with an AI agent](https://gismap.online/guides/ai-agents/): chat-only, code-running and browser-driving recipes
- [AI ArcGIS map generator](https://gismap.online/ai-arcgis-map-generator/): inspect a FeatureServer, style a map, and share a working link
- [ArcGIS FeatureServer viewer](https://gismap.online/arcgis-feature-service-viewer/)

## Worked examples
- [A police divisions briefing, from one prompt or one click](https://gismap.online/examples/ai/philadelphia-police-divisions/): Philadelphia's six police divisions, with the police districts inside them, as a nine-slide interactive briefing on a dark 3D map, opened from one link or QR code.
- [A two-layer briefing with spatial queries, built by an agent](https://gismap.online/examples/ai/mlb-ballparks-by-state/): An AI agent built a ten-slide briefing that shows each state with only the Major League ballparks inside it, using a spatial query per slide, an automatic style and cut transitions.
- [A styled map in one link, written by a chatbot](https://gismap.online/examples/ai/corn-sales-one-link/): Any chatbot, even one that cannot run code, can make a styled county map by writing one JSON object into a link: corn sales by county, with "Not Disclosed" counties kept out of the colour classes.
- [A guided tour of eight classic ballparks](https://gismap.online/examples/tours/classic-ballparks/): A guided tour that flies the 3D map from Fenway Park to Petco Park, with a caption at each of eight ballparks, opened from one link or QR code.
- [A field task and its report, sent as two links](https://gismap.online/examples/field-tasks/opening-day-wayfinding/): A two-ballpark field check sent as a link or QR code, and the completed report that comes back the same way: check-in, steps, features and notes, with no server.

## Data
- [Curated public datasets (JSON)](https://gismap.online/api/catalog.json): 15 services with ready links

## Limits
- At most 10 layers per map; HTTPS only; URLs containing tokens or keys are refused; sources must allow browser (CORS) access.
- Basemaps: topo-3d, navigation-3d, navigation-dark-3d, osm-3d, gray-3d, dark-gray-3d, streets-3d, streets-dark-3d, topo-vector, streets-vector, navigation, gray-vector, dark-gray-vector, osm, satellite, hybrid, usgs-imagery, usgs-imagery-topo, open-liberty, open-bright, open-positron, open-dark, open-fiord, skin.
- Colour ramps: greens, blues, reds, oranges, purples, viridis, magma, red-blue-diverging, brown-teal-diverging.

## Optional
- [Full documentation in one file](https://gismap.online/llms-full.txt)

# Full reference

## Agent guide: Making maps with an AI agent

GIS Map Online opens a map from a link. An agent that can only write text can make a map by writing one JSON object into a URL; agents that run code or drive a browser get validation, statistics and live control. No API key, account or server call is needed.

### 1. Chat-only model: write a link

Look at the service's fields first by opening the layer URL with ?f=pjson appended, and pick a numeric field. Then write a map-v1 spec and put it after #map=json: in the address (URI-encode it when you can).

Worked example: U.S. county corn sales. The publisher's own style labels -1 as "Not Disclosed" (546 of 3,074 counties), so -1 is listed in exclude: those counties are drawn grey as "No data" instead of pulling the colour classes down. sources.inspect reports codes like this as sentinels.

"method": "auto" lets the app choose the class breaks from the data (corn sales are skewed, so it picks quantile classes). Not sure which style suits a field at all? Write { "type": "auto", "field": "CORN_SALES_IN_DOLLARS" } and the app chooses. Saving or sharing from the app records the chosen classes, so the map then looks the same for everyone.

```json
{
  "version": 1,
  "basemap": "gray-vector",
  "layers": [
    {
      "url": "https://services.arcgis.com/P3ePLMYs2RVChkJx/ArcGIS/rest/services/Corn/FeatureServer/0",
      "renderer": {
        "type": "choropleth",
        "field": "CORN_SALES_IN_DOLLARS",
        "method": "auto",
        "ramp": "greens",
        "exclude": [
          -1
        ]
      }
    }
  ]
}
```

Link: https://gismap.online/#map=json:%7B%22version%22%3A1%2C%22basemap%22%3A%22gray-vector%22%2C%22layers%22%3A%5B%7B%22url%22%3A%22https%3A%2F%2Fservices.arcgis.com%2FP3ePLMYs2RVChkJx%2FArcGIS%2Frest%2Fservices%2FCorn%2FFeatureServer%2F0%22%2C%22renderer%22%3A%7B%22type%22%3A%22choropleth%22%2C%22field%22%3A%22CORN_SALES_IN_DOLLARS%22%2C%22method%22%3A%22auto%22%2C%22ramp%22%3A%22greens%22%2C%22exclude%22%3A%5B-1%5D%7D%7D%5D%7D

For one layer and one field there is a shorter form with no JSON: https://gismap.online/?layer=https%3A%2F%2Fservices.arcgis.com%2FP3ePLMYs2RVChkJx%2FArcGIS%2Frest%2Fservices%2FCorn%2FFeatureServer%2F0&layerType=feature&style=choropleth&field=CORN_SALES_IN_DOLLARS&method=auto&ramp=greens&exclude=-1&basemap=gray-vector

### 2. Code-running agent: inspect, validate, link

Import the pure core (a browser, Deno, or Node with a clone of the repository: import ./js/gismap-core.js), inspect the source, validate the spec, and create a link. Python can build the readable link by hand.

```js
import { sources, mapSpec } from "https://gismap.online/js/gismap-core.js";

const url = "https://services.arcgis.com/P3ePLMYs2RVChkJx/ArcGIS/rest/services/Corn/FeatureServer/0";
const meta = await sources.inspect(url); // fields, scale range, freshness, sentinels
const exclude = meta.sentinels
  .filter((code) => code.field === "CORN_SALES_IN_DOLLARS" && code.source !== "heuristic")
  .map((code) => code.value); // [-1]
const spec = { version: 1, basemap: "gray-vector", layers: [{ url, renderer: { type: "choropleth", field: "CORN_SALES_IN_DOLLARS", exclude } }] };
const { valid, issues } = mapSpec.validate(spec);
const { url: link, qr } = await mapSpec.createLink(spec); // compressed; { compress: false } gives #map=json:
```

```python
import json, urllib.parse

spec = {"version": 1, "basemap": "gray-vector", "layers": [{"url": "https://services.arcgis.com/P3ePLMYs2RVChkJx/ArcGIS/rest/services/Corn/FeatureServer/0",
        "renderer": {"type": "choropleth", "field": "CORN_SALES_IN_DOLLARS", "exclude": [-1]}}]}
link = "https://gismap.online/#map=json:" + urllib.parse.quote(json.dumps(spec, separators=(",", ":")), safe="")
```

### 3. Browser-automation agent: drive the page

Wait for gisMapOnline.ready (or the gismap:ready event, or <html data-gismap-state="ready">), add layers, fit the camera, and read describe() to check the result. layers.suggestStyles ranks the styles that suit a field, each with a reason and its class breaks; apply one with its pinnedSpec.

```js
await gisMapOnline.ready;
const layer = await gisMapOnline.layers.add("https://services.arcgis.com/P3ePLMYs2RVChkJx/ArcGIS/rest/services/Corn/FeatureServer/0", {
  renderer: { type: "choropleth", field: "CORN_SALES_IN_DOLLARS", ramp: "greens" }, // sentinels excluded by default
});
await gisMapOnline.camera.fitTo(layer.id);
const { options } = await gisMapOnline.layers.suggestStyles(layer.id, { field: "CORN_SALES_IN_DOLLARS" });
await gisMapOnline.layers.update(layer.id, { renderer: options[0].pinnedSpec }); // the recommended style
console.log(gisMapOnline.describe().state); // layers, basemap, camera, issues
const { url } = await gisMapOnline.mapSpec.createLink(gisMapOnline.mapSpec.fromCurrent());
```

Discover the live registry with gisMapOnline.actions.list() and actions.describe(id). Execute an action with actions.execute({ id, input, expectedRevision }); the revision is optional and only detects changes in the public state projection, not all private or camera changes. Inputs are checked against the declared schema and the existing tool validator before execution; unsupported schema keywords fail closed. Tools without input schemas remain available through the legacy application.runTool but cannot be executed through actions.execute. Outputs are not yet schema-validated; action results can contain session data, so invoke explicitly in a trusted page context. The public state snapshot remains privacy-preserving. This does not provide REST or MCP endpoints.

### Verify the artifact: Michigan county health

Inspect the layer metadata and query actual values before choosing fields. The 2024 County Health Rankings layer 2 is polygon geometry; statecode is a string containing state FIPS, and v001_rawvalue is age-adjusted years of potential life lost per 100,000. On 2026-10-20, statecode = '26' returned 83 Michigan counties. Counts and service availability can change.

Source metadata: https://services.arcgis.com/P3ePLMYs2RVChkJx/ArcGIS/rest/services/County%20Health%20Rankings%202024/FeatureServer/2?f=pjson. Test each where clause using that layer's /query endpoint with f=json and returnCountOnly=true. A successful service query does not prove the GISMap layer loaded, rendered or reopened.

The following filters were accepted by that layer on 2026-10-20. IS NULL tests database null, not missing-value codes; inspect the publisher's metadata and sentinels before deciding which values to exclude. Do not assume other services use these names or codes.

Use mapSpec.prepareVerification(spec) in the browser or core for an offline report; not_checked means exactly that. In a browser, await mapSpec.load(spec).ready, examine issues, layer configuration and rendered features, then open the generated URL in a fresh page and verify again. Report any unavailable steps. Always provide the actual URL, not just a button label.

```sql
statecode = '26'
v001_rawvalue > 0
statecode = '26' AND v001_rawvalue > 0
statecode = '26' AND v001_rawvalue IS NULL
statecode = '26' AND v001_rawvalue IS NOT NULL
```

Michigan share URL (prepared; browser rendering and reopening not independently verified): https://gismap.online/#map=json:%7B%22version%22%3A1%2C%22title%22%3A%22Michigan%20county%20health%22%2C%22basemap%22%3A%22gray-vector%22%2C%22camera%22%3A%7B%22center%22%3A%5B-85.5%2C44.6%5D%2C%22zoom%22%3A5.5%7D%2C%22layers%22%3A%5B%7B%22url%22%3A%22https%3A%2F%2Fservices.arcgis.com%2FP3ePLMYs2RVChkJx%2FArcGIS%2Frest%2Fservices%2FCounty%2520Health%2520Rankings%25202024%2FFeatureServer%2F2%22%2C%22type%22%3A%22feature%22%2C%22where%22%3A%22statecode%20%3D%20'26'%22%2C%22renderer%22%3A%7B%22type%22%3A%22choropleth%22%2C%22field%22%3A%22v001_rawvalue%22%2C%22method%22%3A%22quantile%22%2C%22classes%22%3A5%2C%22ramp%22%3A%22greens%22%7D%7D%5D%7D

Prepared: spec or URL constructed. Validated: GISMap's validator accepted it (review warnings). Loaded: required layers loaded in the application. Verified: intended features, filter, style and camera were confirmed, including reopening the share link. Do not imply a later stage was completed when it was not.

### Refine an existing map into multiple views

Choose the simplest working interface: simple ?layer= parameters for basic filtering and a supported style; map-v1 JSON for independent layers, categorized colors, camera, opacity and legends; or the in-page API for the currently open map. Do not stop at advice when a requested change can be expressed declaratively.

For an existing #map= link use mapSpec.decode(payload), which also handles supported compressed map payloads. For a simple ?layer= URL, parseShareParameters and mapSpec.fromShareParameters reconstruct the spec. For a hosted ?spec= fetch the trusted file; for an open map use gisMapOnline.mapSpec.fromCurrent(). If compressed decoding is unavailable, ask for the original JSON or an uncompressed #map=json: link rather than guessing. Preserve filters, camera and basemap, check validation warnings, and don't replace the user's source with a different one.

The example begins with a California historical fire-perimeters filter and derives two independent maps. On 2026-10-20 the layer metadata identified polygon geometry, numeric YEAR_ and GIS_ACRES fields, and its service accepted the filter. These links are prepared and statically validated; rendered styles and share-link reopening still need a browser check.

```js
import { mapSpec } from "https://gismap.online/js/gismap-core.js";
import { parseShareParameters } from "https://gismap.online/js/share.js";
const previous = new URL("https://gismap.online/?layer=https%3A%2F%2Fservices1.arcgis.com%2FjUJYIo9tSA7EHvfZ%2FArcGIS%2Frest%2Fservices%2FCalifornia_Historic_Fire_Perimeters%2FFeatureServer%2F0&layerType=feature&where=YEAR_%20%3E%3D%202000%20AND%20YEAR_%20%3C%3D%202010&basemap=gray-vector&center=-120%2C37.5&level=5");
const payload = new URLSearchParams(previous.hash.slice(1)).get("map");
const base = payload ? await mapSpec.decode(payload) : mapSpec.fromShareParameters(parseShareParameters(previous.search));
const colors = ["#8e0152", "#d73027", "#f46d43", "#fdae61", "#fee08b", "#66a61e", "#1b9e77", "#1f78b4", "#6a3d9a", "#a6761d", "#4d4d4d"];
const year = structuredClone(base), acres = structuredClone(base);
year.layers[0].renderer = { type: "categories", field: "YEAR_", maxCategories: 11, colors: Object.fromEntries(colors.map((c, i) => [String(2000 + i), c])) };
acres.layers[0].renderer = { type: "choropleth", field: "GIS_ACRES", classes: 5, method: "quantile", classColors: ["#ffffb2", "#fecc5c", "#fd8d3c", "#f03b20", "#bd0026"] };
for (const spec of [year, acres]) {
  const report = await mapSpec.prepareVerification(spec);
  console.log(report.url, report.checks, report.warnings, report.errors);
}
```

Inspect source fields and validate both renderers against them; then open each URL in GISMap, confirm the filter, map, legend, categories and acreage classes, and reopen it. Category and class generation can use sampled data. A generated URL alone is not verified. Numeric year-slider authoring is not defined in map-v1; treat it as an enhancement rather than claiming support.

Prepared examples and source JSON: https://gismap.online/examples/ai/california-fire-refinement/

### 4. Handling errors

Every error from the API is a GisMapError with a code and a hint written for agents. When a map spec opens, problems are listed in describe().state.issues instead of stopping the map.

| Code | What to do |
| --- | --- |
| `INVALID_URL` | Pass a complete https:// URL to a service, layer or file. |
| `HTTPS_REQUIRED` | Use the https:// form of the URL; GIS Map Online only loads remote data over HTTPS. |
| `CREDENTIAL_IN_URL` | Remove the token, key or password from the URL. Only public services can be shared. |
| `UNSUPPORTED_LAYER_TYPE` | Use one of the layer types listed in capabilities.json (arcgis-auto, feature, map-image, imagery, geojson, wms, wfs, kml). |
| `TOO_MANY_LAYERS` | A map holds at most 10 data layers. Remove one with layers.remove before adding another. |
| `LAYER_LOAD_FAILED` | Check the URL in a browser with ?f=pjson appended. The service may be down, private or not a layer URL. |
| `CORS_BLOCKED` | The publisher does not allow browser access to this service. Use another source, or download the data and add it as a file. |
| `SERVICE_ERROR` | The service answered with an error. Check the URL, the layer number and any filter for typos. |
| `FIELD_NOT_FOUND` | Use a field name exactly as the service lists it; sources.inspect(url) returns the fields. |
| `INVALID_SPEC` | Fix the listed issues; the schema in capabilities.json describes every property. |
| `NOT_READY` | Await gisMapOnline.ready before calling this. |
| `NOT_FOUND` | Call layers.list() to see the layers on the map and their ids. |
| `SPEC_TOO_LONG` | Shorten the spec (fewer layers, no raw ArcGIS renderers) or use the compressed #map= form from mapSpec.createLink, or host the JSON and link to it with ?spec=. |

### 5. Data caveats

- Sentinels: some services store codes such as -1 or -9999 for "not disclosed" or "no data". sources.inspect and layers.list() report them; statistics leave them out and choropleths draw them as "No data". Sample-based guesses (source: heuristic) are reported but never applied.
- Scale ranges: a publisher can hide a layer above or below a scale (Corn hides itself zoomed in past 1:144,447). Set ignoreServiceScaleRange: true to draw it at every zoom.
- Record limits: services return at most maxRecordCount features per request. Statistics computed from loaded features are labelled as a sample when the layer has more.
- Freshness: sources.inspect and layers.list() give dataLastEditDate; say how current the data is when you describe it.
- Access: services must be public, HTTPS and allow browser (CORS) access. URLs with tokens or keys are refused.

## Map spec (map-v1)

A whole map as one JSON object: layers with styles and filters, basemap, look and camera. Open it at https://gismap.online/#map=json:<URI-encoded JSON> (written by hand, up to 8 KB), as the compressed #map= form from mapSpec.createLink, or host the file and open https://gismap.online/?spec=<https URL>. Invalid parts are skipped and reported; the rest of the map still opens.

Top-level properties:

- `version`: The spec version. Always 1.
- `title`: The map's name, shown as the project title.
- `description`: What the map shows, for people reading the spec.
- `basemap`: The background map. gray-vector and dark-gray-vector keep attention on the data; the open-* basemaps are OpenFreeMap styles (MapLibre engine; ArcGIS draws the nearest match); skin draws it in the colours of the interface skin (with the MapLibre engine; the ArcGIS engine uses the light or dark gray canvas). One of: topo-3d, navigation-3d, navigation-dark-3d, osm-3d, gray-3d, dark-gray-3d, streets-3d, streets-dark-3d, topo-vector, streets-vector, navigation, gray-vector, dark-gray-vector, osm, satellite, hybrid, usgs-imagery, usgs-imagery-topo, open-liberty, open-bright, open-positron, open-dark, open-fiord, skin.
- `skin`: The interface look. It never changes a layer's style; with the skin basemap the map is drawn in its colours, and with the MapLibre engine layers that have no style take its accent colour. One of: gismap, clean-light, dark-analytical, tidal-95, portolan, velvet-orbit, violet-circuit, highway, steeler, slice, wavelength, connect.
- `camera`: Where the map looks. Default { "fit": "layers" }: fit the loaded data (its dense core when it spreads over half the world).
- `layers`: The data, drawn in order (the last is on top). At most 10.
- `legend`: Open the legend.
- `briefing`: Optional slides that present the map, as a briefing-v1 document (https://gismap.online/schemas/briefing-v1.schema.json). Its layerId may be one of the layer URLs.

Layer properties:

- `layers[].url`: HTTPS URL of an ArcGIS REST layer or service (FeatureServer/0, MapServer, ImageServer), a GeoJSON file, or a WMS/WFS/KML service. Public only: no tokens or keys. The service must allow browser (CORS) access. Append ?f=pjson to an ArcGIS URL to see its fields.
- `layers[].type`: The layer type; arcgis-auto detects it from the service, and from .las/.laz/.xyz (pointcloud) or .glb/.gltf/.obj/.ply (model) file extensions. pointcloud and model draw with three.js on the MapLibre engine. One of: arcgis-auto, feature, map-image, imagery, geojson, geoparquet, wms, wfs, kml, pointcloud, model.
- `layers[].title`: The name shown in the Layers panel and legend.
- `layers[].where`: A read-only SQL filter on the layer's fields, such as "CORN_SALES_IN_DOLLARS >= 0" or "STATE = 'Iowa'". No statements, comments or semicolons.
- `layers[].renderer`: The style. Field names must match the service exactly; a misspelled field keeps the service's own style and is reported.
- `layers[].scene3d`: Options for pointcloud and model layers (MapLibre engine, drawn with three.js). Elevations are real heights in metres after unit conversion, not virtual Z.
- `layers[].animatedEffect`: Decorative animated effect drawn on the layer's features (MapLibre engine; other engines show the layer without it). It is visual annotation, never data. auto picks one from the layer's title, geometry and fields; pulse sizes rings by a magnitude field and wind follows direction/speed fields when present.
- `layers[].spatialChart`: 3D spatial chart settings (MapLibre and ArcGIS engines). Z values are display offsets, never physical altitude. source-footprints/none is the fast display strategy and does not calculate exact polygon overlaps.
- `layers[].opacity`: 0 is transparent, 1 is opaque.
- `layers[].visible`: Whether the layer starts switched on.
- `layers[].ignoreServiceScaleRange`: Draw at every zoom level, even where the publisher hides the layer (its minScale/maxScale).
- `layers[].refreshInterval`: Reload the layer every this many minutes (for live feeds).
- `layers[].popup`: Fields of interest for inspecting features.

## RendererSpec (styles)

A declarative layer style. GIS Map Online compiles it to an ArcGIS renderer, computing class breaks from the layer's data. Not sure which style suits a field? Use { "type": "auto", "field": ... } or "method": "auto" and the app decides from the data. Field names must match the service's fields exactly (sources.inspect(url).fields lists them).

- `service`: Keep the publisher's own style (the default).
- `simple`: One colour for every feature. Properties: color, outline, size.
- `choropleth`: Colour features by a numeric field in classes (a choropleth for polygons). Values listed in exclude, and nulls, are drawn grey as "No data" and kept out of the classes. Properties: field, classes, method, breaks, ramp, reverseRamp, classColors, normalizeBy, exclude.
- `graduated-symbols`: Size point or line symbols by a numeric field. Polygon layers get a choropleth instead (with a warning). Properties: field, classes, method, breaks, color, ramp, reverseRamp, classColors, minSize, maxSize, exclude.
- `categories`: One colour per value of a field (the most common values; the rest are "Other"). Properties: field, maxCategories, colors.
- `heatmap`: A heat map of point density, optionally weighted by a numeric field. Point layers only. Properties: field.
- `arcgis`: Raw ArcGIS renderer JSON, for styles the other types cannot express. Properties: json.
- `auto`: Let the app choose the style from the data when the map opens: colours or sized symbols with the break method that suits the values (quantile for skewed values, natural breaks for clusters, equal interval for even spreads), or categories for a text field. Without a field, the most measurement-like field is used. Saving or sharing from the app records the chosen style with its breaks. Properties: field, classes, ramp, exclude.

Named ramps: greens, blues, reds, oranges, purples, viridis, magma, red-blue-diverging, brown-teal-diverging.

## URL parameters

Query (after ?):

- `layer`: HTTPS URL of a public layer, service or GeoJSON file. No tokens or keys. Example: `https://services.arcgis.com/P3ePLMYs2RVChkJx/ArcGIS/rest/services/Corn/FeatureServer/0`.
- `layerType` (index-aligned with layer): Layer type; arcgis-auto detects it. Values: arcgis-auto, feature, map-image, imagery, geojson, geoparquet, wms, wfs, kml, pointcloud, model. Example: `feature`.
- `title` (index-aligned with layer): Layer title. Example: `Corn sales`.
- `where` (index-aligned with layer): Read-only SQL filter on the layer's fields. Example: `CORN_SALES_IN_DOLLARS >= 0`.
- `style` (index-aligned with layer): A style without JSON. Values: service, simple, choropleth, graduated, categories, heatmap, auto. Example: `choropleth`.
- `field` (index-aligned with layer): The field a style uses (exactly as the service names it). Example: `CORN_SALES_IN_DOLLARS`.
- `classes` (index-aligned with layer): Number of classes for choropleth and graduated styles. Example: `5`.
- `method` (index-aligned with layer): How class breaks are chosen; auto picks from the values (quantile when skewed, natural breaks when clustered, equal interval when even). Values: natural-breaks, quantile, equal-interval, auto. Example: `auto`.
- `breaks` (index-aligned with layer): Comma-separated class upper bounds, for fixed classes that look the same whenever the map opens. Example: `1000000,10000000,50000000`.
- `ramp` (index-aligned with layer): A named colour ramp. Values: greens, blues, reds, oranges, purples, viridis, magma, red-blue-diverging, brown-teal-diverging. Example: `greens`.
- `exclude` (index-aligned with layer): Comma-separated codes drawn as "No data" and kept out of the classes. Example: `-1`.
- `color` (index-aligned with layer): Hex colour for simple and graduated styles. Example: `d9951e`.
- `opacity` (index-aligned with layer): 0 (transparent) to 1 (opaque). Example: `0.8`.
- `basemap`: The background map, applied before the scene starts. Values: topo-3d, navigation-3d, navigation-dark-3d, osm-3d, gray-3d, dark-gray-3d, streets-3d, streets-dark-3d, topo-vector, streets-vector, navigation, gray-vector, dark-gray-vector, osm, satellite, hybrid, usgs-imagery, usgs-imagery-topo, open-liberty, open-bright, open-positron, open-dark, open-fiord, skin. Example: `gray-vector`.
- `zoom`: layers fits the loaded data; none keeps the starting view. Values: layers, none. Example: `none`.
- `center`: View centre in degrees; use with scale or level. Example: `-93.6,42`.
- `scale`: Map scale denominator, with center. Example: `500000`.
- `level`: Zoom level, with center. Example: `7`.
- `example`: A curated dataset (see /api/catalog.json). Values: usa-wildfires, modis-active-fires, active-hurricanes, recent-hurricanes, air-quality-pm25, air-quality-pm25-3d-columns, air-quality-pm25-3d-graduated, usgs-seismic-activity, usgs-recent-earthquakes-map-service, ndfd-wind-gusts, ndfd-precipitation, ndfd-daily-temperature, historical-quakes, usgs-earthquakes, world-countries-generalized. Example: `usa-wildfires`.
- `spec`: HTTPS URL of a CORS-enabled map-v1 JSON file. Example: `https://example.org/corn.map.json`.
- `briefing`: HTTPS URL of a briefing file (briefing-v1 document, project or the app's briefing file). Example: `https://example.org/corn.briefing.json`.

Fragment (after #):

- `map`: json:<URI-encoded map-v1 JSON> (readable, at most 8192 characters) or the compressed z… form from mapSpec.createLink. Example: `json:%7B%22version%22%3A1%2C%22basemap%22%3A%22gray-vector%22%2C%22layers%22%3A%5B%7B%22url%22%3A%22https%3A%2F%2Fservices.arcgis.com%2FP3ePLMYs2RVChkJx%2FArcGIS%2Frest%2Fservices%2FCorn%2FFeatureServer%2F0%22%2C%22renderer%22%3A%7B%22type%22%3A%22choropleth%22%2C%22field%22%3A%22CORN_SALES_IN_DOLLARS%22%2C%22method%22%3A%22auto%22%2C%22ramp%22%3A%22greens%22%2C%22exclude%22%3A%5B-1%5D%7D%7D%5D%7D`.
- `briefing`: A briefing link payload (from the app or briefing.createLink).
- `slide`: Open a briefing at this slide id.

## Error codes

- `INVALID_URL`: Pass a complete https:// URL to a service, layer or file.
- `HTTPS_REQUIRED`: Use the https:// form of the URL; GIS Map Online only loads remote data over HTTPS.
- `CREDENTIAL_IN_URL`: Remove the token, key or password from the URL. Only public services can be shared.
- `UNSUPPORTED_LAYER_TYPE`: Use one of the layer types listed in capabilities.json (arcgis-auto, feature, map-image, imagery, geojson, wms, wfs, kml).
- `TOO_MANY_LAYERS`: A map holds at most 10 data layers. Remove one with layers.remove before adding another.
- `LAYER_LOAD_FAILED`: Check the URL in a browser with ?f=pjson appended. The service may be down, private or not a layer URL.
- `CORS_BLOCKED`: The publisher does not allow browser access to this service. Use another source, or download the data and add it as a file.
- `SERVICE_ERROR`: The service answered with an error. Check the URL, the layer number and any filter for typos.
- `FIELD_NOT_FOUND`: Use a field name exactly as the service lists it; sources.inspect(url) returns the fields.
- `INVALID_SPEC`: Fix the listed issues; the schema in capabilities.json describes every property.
- `NOT_READY`: Await gisMapOnline.ready before calling this.
- `NOT_FOUND`: Call layers.list() to see the layers on the map and their ids.
- `SPEC_TOO_LONG`: Shorten the spec (fewer layers, no raw ArcGIS renderers) or use the compressed #map= form from mapSpec.createLink, or host the JSON and link to it with ?spec=.

## In-page API (globalThis.gisMapOnline)

Language models and agents start at [`/llms.txt`](https://gismap.online/llms.txt) (the whole reference is in [`/llms-full.txt`](https://gismap.online/llms-full.txt)) and the guide [Making maps with an AI agent](https://gismap.online/guides/ai-agents/), with recipes for a chat-only model, a code-running agent and a browser-driving agent. [Worked examples](https://gismap.online/examples/ai/) show chatbots and agents making real maps and briefings, with their prompts, code, links and QR codes. [`/api/url-parameters.json`](api/url-parameters.json) and [`/api/catalog.json`](api/catalog.json) list every link parameter and the curated datasets. These files are generated by `node scripts/build-examples.mjs` and readable from any origin.

Everything an agent needs is on `globalThis.gisMapOnline` once `await gisMapOnline.ready` resolves (also a `gismap:ready` event and `<html data-gismap-state="ready">`):

```js
const api = globalThis.gisMapOnline;
await api.ready;
const corn = await api.layers.add("https://services.arcgis.com/P3ePLMYs2RVChkJx/ArcGIS/rest/services/Corn/FeatureServer/0", {
  renderer: { type: "choropleth", field: "CORN_SALES_IN_DOLLARS", ramp: "greens" }, // -1 "Not Disclosed" goes to "No data"
});
await api.camera.fitTo(corn.id);
api.describe(); // capabilities + live layers, basemap, camera, skin, mode
await api.application.runTool("layer.filter", { layer: corn.id, where: "CORN_SALES_IN_DOLLARS >= 0" });
```

### A map from one JSON object (no code)

A chat-only model can make a map by writing a [map-v1](schemas/map-v1.schema.json) spec and URI-encoding it into a link:

```text
https://gismap.online/#map=json:{"version":1,"basemap":"gray-vector","layers":[{"url":"https://services.arcgis.com/P3ePLMYs2RVChkJx/ArcGIS/rest/services/Corn/FeatureServer/0","renderer":{"type":"choropleth","field":"CORN_SALES_IN_DOLLARS","method":"auto","ramp":"greens","exclude":[-1]}}]}
```

URI-encode the JSON (`encodeURIComponent`) when you can; the readable form holds up to 8,192 characters. `gisMapOnline.mapSpec.createLink(spec)` (or `mapSpec.createLink` from `js/gismap-core.js`) gives the compressed `#map=` form, and `?spec=<https URL>` opens a hosted spec. For one layer and one field there is no JSON at all: `?layer=<URL>&style=choropleth&field=<FIELD>&method=auto&ramp=greens&exclude=-1&basemap=gray-vector`. Invalid parts are skipped and listed in `describe().state.issues`.

`"method": "auto"` lets the app choose the class breaks from the data (quantile for skewed values, natural breaks for clusters, equal interval for even spreads), and `{ "type": "auto", "field": "…" }` (`style=auto`) lets it choose the whole style. `breaks: [1000, 50000, …]` fixes the classes. When the app resolves an `auto` style it records the result with its breaks, so saved projects and shared links look the same for everyone. `gisMapOnline.layers.suggestStyles(id, { field })` (and the Style options list in the style panel) ranks the styles that suit a field, each with a reason, its breaks and a `pinnedSpec` to apply; `renderers.suggest` in `js/gismap-core.js` does the same from values you pass in.

Errors are `GisMapError` with a `code` and a `hint` written for agents. The contracts are [`api/capabilities.json`](api/capabilities.json) (namespaces, stability, tools with input schemas, error codes, ramps, basemaps, URL parameters), [`schemas/renderer-v1.schema.json`](schemas/renderer-v1.schema.json) and [`js/gismap-core.d.ts`](js/gismap-core.d.ts) (`InPageApi`). A `?layer=` link zooms to its data unless it says `zoom=none` or gives `center=lon,lat&level=` / `&scale=`.

## Briefing API

GISMap exposes the same versioned Briefing functions to in-page agents and to ES-module callers. No GISMap server or account is required.

```js
const api = globalThis.gisMapOnline;
const slide = api.briefing.createSlide("map-narrative", {
  title: "Where improvements are planned",
});
const document = api.briefing.addSlide(api.briefing.create(), slide);

api.briefing.load(document); // opens the document in Briefing
// The same link the app shares: it opens the slides with the map's layers,
// styles, filters, skin and view. { documentOnly: true } gives a slides-only
// link (#briefing=b1.…) that applies to whatever layers the URL loads (?layer=…).
const link = await api.briefing.createLink(document, { qrSafe: true });
const project = api.briefing.exportGmo(document); // { fileName, mimeType, text, blob }

// Build slides from the map as it looks (style, filter, chosen features), and render the PDF handout.
await api.briefing.generate({ layerId: "https://…/FeatureServer/0", ai: true });
const pdf = await api.briefing.exportPdf(); // File
const qrCard = await api.briefing.exportQrCard(); // branded PNG File
```

The experimental in-page `briefing.generateTemplate` API previews or appends Filter Series, Timeline, Grid Atlas, and 3D Spatial Chart slides from an already loaded layer. It queries at most 500 features and reports coverage as unknown; its statistics are not guaranteed complete. Set `previewOnly: true` to avoid saving. It is not a standalone core or HTTP API. See [data-driven briefing API](https://gismap.online/skills/gismap/references/briefs.md) for options, geometry limits, and verification guidance.

A briefing document can say which data it is about: `layerId` is best given as the layer's service URL, which GISMap loads if it is not already on the map, and `selection.ids` lists the chosen features. Host a document as JSON (CORS-enabled) and link to it as `https://gismap.online/?briefing=<file URL>`; GISMap opens it on that layer and starts presenting. The file may be a briefing document, a project that contains one, or the briefing file the share dialog downloads.

Headless agents can import the pure core without opening the app:

```js
import { briefing, sources } from "./js/gismap-core.js";

const metadata = await sources.inspect("https://example.org/arcgis/rest/services/Projects/FeatureServer/0");
const result = briefing.validate(document);
```

The machine-readable contracts are [`api/capabilities.json`](api/capabilities.json), [`schemas/briefing-v1.schema.json`](schemas/briefing-v1.schema.json), and the [`gismap-core` TypeScript declarations](js/gismap-core.d.ts). Filters, slides, blocks, cameras and styles are declarative data; credentials and temporary viewer state do not belong in a briefing. Browser source inspection remains subject to CORS. The library does not provide hosted links, access control, or background jobs.

### Smart map images

Project → Download project can create a **Smart map image**: a polished, standards-compliant PNG containing the complete editable project configuration in GISMap's private `giMp` ancillary chunk. The visible image opens normally anywhere; importing the original PNG through Project → Import restores its camera, basemap, public layer references, styling, bookmarks, workflows, and Briefing slides.

```js
const output = await gisMapOnline.smartImages.createCurrent();
const manifest = await gisMapOnline.smartImages.read(output.blob);
console.log(output.file.name, output.share?.url, output.share?.qr);

await gisMapOnline.smartImages.downloadCurrent();
```

`createCurrent()` gives an agent the PNG without forcing a browser download and also returns `share`, the equivalent live-map link with public layers, styles, filters, camera, basemap, and skin. `createShareLink()` returns that link directly. Its `qr` flag says whether it fits safely in GISMap's separate branded QR image. Keeping the QR as a separate artifact leaves the Smart Image clean while providing a reliable route back to the live map; GISMap can also reopen QR screenshots and photos.

The embedded payload is versioned, deflate-compressed when supported, protected by PNG CRC and SHA-256 integrity checks, and bounded by explicit input limits. Remote URLs containing credentials are rejected. Smart Images reference public services and do not make those services offline; use `.gmop` when local datasets must travel with the project. Keep the original PNG—social networks and image editors may resize it or remove ancillary metadata. When another service strips the private PNG chunk, share the companion live link or QR image alongside it.

### Composable application preview

Feature branches under `codex/**` run `.github/workflows/development-preview.yml`. Every run produces a 14-day static preview artifact after the complete test suite and JavaScript syntax checks pass. An isolated Cloudflare Pages development deployment is enabled only when the `development` GitHub environment defines `CLOUDFLARE_PAGES_PROJECT_DEV`, `CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN_DEV`, and `CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID_DEV`. These names deliberately do not reuse production credentials or destinations, and the workflow has no production trigger.

The production site remains unchanged until its separate release process is explicitly invoked.

## Worked examples

### A police divisions briefing, from one prompt or one click

Chatbot. Philadelphia's six police divisions, with the police districts inside them, as a nine-slide interactive briefing on a dark 3D map, opened from one link or QR code.

Open it: https://gismap.online/#briefing=zzVbbbts4EP0VgY-BLIuUqNubkThtFk7WiIsWi6IwKImyCOtikHRSN_B39b1ftkPZbm0r2Cx2gcIQbGo4M5w5hzOkXtATSrCNlihBqRS8EM0C2UiDOG0rkXHrRjwJJdpGwbSC6VIsyme2AakGqWFPYsE06Ac5k8uBl4MiQ8mL-fs8CKmDvTiMbS92Yuri4IuNvkFA4oQ2KlHiBW4XjPiOv7XRBHxe0NpE0XqlkuFQcfkEWSiHyWwhlJO19XDq8enk_i9FHj9el8s_vg5HMnt3NxtKrvRPh-G0FBXLebUqBZtfS1Hz-T1bzT_dTvDwljO9lnwGtlwOMaS8gZjFbhak5nX40uDSmxUHtRL1qjK2alOnbXWk4UqK2e3M8NBWLfh89ogdYhvjyPZ9IKBd60o0_NxlcuyCaWQffoRS8HoWuQbGsIMJhah6Ux15ziDZHG3P5m8P89tu6_DW_v3kkn8mV2kpMv1_yHXt7vm3vAbAaUhtHMVnvP4HTluUuE5It7DKCl5tlJrYCtRcdZUMdgBmkBNOSUYj01gckDFtltNCdxh34-v9tk4P2sA611s_vlt_ZrpNubQwtS3iksAgZTWXrOtA3mguj9vQpy6lIabevh89H0c-wXFAQtOYbVt3vemHrhe5BMOCJA486FTOcnMwJB4Fvzgi2AtCGoZRZNKvdg3shbBySKkXuq4fAz1p1WbLHRH7_dD8qzYHB5wUeftsCuFDya2arSxVts_Kuro6B3l15aDtF1O4ey6jLHAJz-JTLpd8M2jWNVChjhgdaYtZi4o1meG5n47SzKTTDQmUyLoxYsVSXr22Hyd5BF4RpZji0zx-Vfkhh-vpDUj7-Tvja1wKoU-s-7kVbNcWheBVbjRoOn68ux9_GD_C7M3dx_nD6H4Mr7P3o-l4PuHduT0r2YrP5yPJ2S_J6KDEu-yPN-IED8dZ5BZR-BaecQ8PuUg8RQyV6_n8LTwPfUDeRQLyA5_HLntzgx4-9QD5FwmooFlAo_Ssk_uAZj089CLxxHGYBRnN38TT36DgIgHBOQt3QHDWQpDE_nb6WXHgaSnNV8piTW6pdi3hG-FVCBVc-OgoKNzXS2O5G43h4fS9YZolvTsPTNfSqH_nJww2tJjHRsx8Rf0N

Page: https://gismap.online/examples/ai/philadelphia-police-divisions/

What it shows:

- Two layers in one briefing: the divisions it is about, and the districts as context
- A slide per division, each framed on its feature, with its attributes
- A key number computed from the data (six divisions)
- A full briefing link that carries the layers, styles, 3D basemap, look and camera with the slides
- A QR code that opens the same presentation on a phone

Prompt for a chatbot:

> Use GISMap.online to make an interactive briefing of Philadelphia's police divisions. Main layer: https://services.arcgis.com/P3ePLMYs2RVChkJx/ArcGIS/rest/services/Philadelphia_Crime_Map_WFL1/FeatureServer/1 (Police_Divisions). Second layer, as context: https://services.arcgis.com/P3ePLMYs2RVChkJx/ArcGIS/rest/services/Philadelphia_Crime_Map_WFL1/FeatureServer/2 (Police_Districts) at 75% opacity. Do not load the crime incident points (layer 0). Slides: a title slide, an "At a glance" slide counting the divisions, one feature slide per division framed on it (DIV_NAME is the division name), and a sources slide linking the layers. Use a dark 3D basemap. Write it as one map-v1 spec with the briefing inside (https://gismap.online/schemas/map-v1.schema.json, https://gismap.online/schemas/briefing-v1.schema.json; see https://gismap.online/guides/ai-agents/) and return the link and a QR code. Do not invent crime totals or imply the boundaries are current.

For a code-running agent: An agent with Node, Deno or a browser writes the map and its slides as one map-v1 spec, validates it, and makes the link with the GISMap core. A link whose spec carries slides opens presenting them.

```js
import { mapSpec } from "https://gismap.online/js/gismap-core.js";

// Two layers, a dark 3D basemap and the nine slides (see map.json for the full spec).
const spec = await (await fetch("https://gismap.online/examples/ai/philadelphia-police-divisions/map.json")).json();
// spec.layers: [{ url: ".../FeatureServer/1", title: "Police Divisions" },
//               { url: ".../FeatureServer/2", title: "Police Districts", opacity: 0.75 }]
// spec.briefing.slides: title, "At a glance", one { template: "feature", featureId, fit: "feature" } per division, sources

const { valid, issues } = mapSpec.validate(spec); // check before sharing
const { url, qr } = await mapSpec.createLink(spec); // qr: true when the link fits a QR code
```

Caveats:

- The layers show police division and district boundaries, not reported crime. No slide shows crime rates or incident counts.
- The division slides list the layer's fields as published: DIV_NAME, and geometry measurements such as PERIMETER and Shape__Area.
- The source layers were last edited on September 22, 2021; check for newer boundaries before operational use.

### A two-layer briefing with spatial queries, built by an agent

AI agent. An AI agent built a ten-slide briefing that shows each state with only the Major League ballparks inside it, using a spatial query per slide, an automatic style and cut transitions.

Open it: https://gismap.online/#map=z5Zltb9s2EID_CsF96BYojmVbtqN9coKuS5c0Xp0MGIYgOFEniwtFaiRl1wv8u_Z9v2wg5Re5axMv6AuGAI2jVEf5Xp67I0_3dIbacCVpHAbUciuQxvQCfleanCNMKyQJCFGCvjMkWRBjwSINaAIGCyhpTKcaFoczZFZpGlAGBWqg8T3NuKUxFbBAbegyWF_Fv93TSgsa09za0sRHRwb1jDM0LdBsyk2LqeJo3MXx-cWvpvP2l9P87vW7o_rekUZjNwuOriej24lTyNy-QokaBP8T09sTVckUNEdz9AOCrTROUM9QH7VpQO2idBbWzzuEyiq6tfu6NWnVJhoaUI0yRY3aWbNaxnKlVSnQ5jSgGUeR0piOL8e3k58vzpz5AoxBQ-MooAXaXLn7qy_RUDh_JaJC7xBVAuN2QeN2a7AMPp1XfPBu6-DdnoBBF0Dnp5RXxX92ycX5yZaAjzgFLE6V83fDKecvR6-uX9KAFvDudCsQh-2AMiWUQ-GejgrUnIGkMf2GDcN2x7H1BixXEpw3vmm3O-mgQ5fL5U1AE80x43LqVhqWYwG_NOD1gJ2lX40sgwKZ9drcU5461GlEA9rr0YCGTqLbdR_H7qNPA9pxH2GP3iwDagRPsc4O7kwwh3UAAmqxKIVLuphu_mvvNDVVsha-mitS52BAlESydib5-y9SQIpuGUgyOiMwRWl3cpmhtC7kvx0e94PusBXdBPRPpQoad1v9gOYIqQ9L2-kmLI3by4AmQrG72qQVKBbfWU-EvkvV3AW99jEBjcTkkGLqtDg4KFVZCU8BSVEabhcHB983LHTyDqJKr1cI74SDgxZ5CSyv7SfeqcTkam6IkmJBbN70E5fG3bc52HpBiwa195PDQRImLMI-ddxldawdW7ISIqhrW30plSsWMaUBzXmaoqRxBsKgy-hVJBkIniktOeyGc_XYRkBPm5KNb_Uc1QV1u-jf_s2A2U0Oev4mV6Orl7dvRhcuE8eX4-vz0dXZ5Zv6j7po3WxsDqOoPRgMkTrdPxqyk7X_YpLxGRKLUJjAu7ZQxhKVEZArAlvk8qNu39q6Cr-aS_KtKcFyEERjHX-T8zImTEkLXJrvGhEahr2k3e2kPkKN5uIvv04hnXHDExdIqyt0pbK2oVkqV4ZQX88a2dlIt725svgOzGNIXa2EmjT5ivTZcTqGYcR6MNwbpx9VZaySBGRKRlpwObVKPoSQt-1p9CRRD9NwkDxfejKhNE8fLUk_bMSaBPl29tkJGkTdKGEs2pugCw4F9_xMbIuM0aI2SaWnD0G0MvBpGGE3Gw7TfvZ8MZI4P1woffcYR29wTn6t5Zog-S3RZwcpSY6HvTDcH6RE2ZxwSdZak1NuFw9RtBF8EkbdKEtYxtrPF6MSpTQLMYM9dknjXdkdnI6_CE7tYdbLOu29cRrnXECKoszdbkemZMyt9ZUpfwiqpqFPAwu6w0HU7z9jsFTO1WNAXdYyOyD1vwRI7TCDQTjM9gbpVOAMhSPI_ZxyybiUYHmrcf3CECdNDLfu2OPRchaSt3yGut6p1-cjwSUGxChic25Wp6WpdqclL-8PViEpuMCDA5JgpjQSMHfu0DjPOcubxNoNfw38Oqzb6afA_p_4BTTlxoJk6OcLleTWweb88WnYLLgxqtL8MT4vtnJNRjtfhNFOGqa9HuvvzehPIA0Y3zE3W7FzVXHzUKlbm_i0Mnc8jAb9QdT9f3L2KVDiQnCp-KPHwbOt3M5-_oucCLv97rAT9fcvd-tt2GnOGUzVQwCtDXviMKEdpsdJFj1fgHI132UH_CzTNNj5Uc3rTrEZHc7BkKRyE7_PMC0U3LjncouFR-0CuKwnmDFpDOpb5NLmqNd3dubVARG84BZT1wfx_cGgG3iSNSN_VKgXxKr36No2y2Z7u8qRTLdzYaIq63qpIWVldzvx-knBhzrx75Wxa35_QmkrdrdY9eOV4Id6ct2RSca1sU6ZV1rNXTA2GeB1hgLJHBZkriqRkrISwiXSpha_MOSkMiwnKwIJMK1MvdbVYvevLLnXxo9O_bdz43WR7mvfqilqQ05RWo3k2yullbSKnIgKyWtYmO-ctMtdkJCCf5BUHxjMcm_ExM-_CassSdDOEeUqvESDD6_NQZJMLJylDV2ZqqTVi1azYTHMcBilzSojuPRvL-rfdWYn6N4wXE9GZDWFbkz6yXbST4Ov-L7KmbDWdGfav64g6_h9SjX_Y6laNgY2YcIgxXq_t1uQnjRDvwmo1eBeAPjKR1nlKoJLVf8u6X65XP4D

Page: https://gismap.online/examples/ai/mlb-ballparks-by-state/

What it shows:

- Other layers on each slide: the ballparks are shown with the states and limited per slide
- Spatial relationships as the ArcGIS REST API defines them (contains), with a distance where needed
- "method": "auto": the states' population density classes are chosen from the data
- "transition": "cut": slides jump between states instead of flying across the country
- A whole map and briefing in one map-v1 spec, opened from one link or QR code

Prompt for a chatbot:

> Make a GISMap.online briefing of Major League ballparks by state. Main layer: https://services.arcgis.com/P3ePLMYs2RVChkJx/arcgis/rest/services/USA_States_Generalized_Boundaries/FeatureServer/0 (shade POP_SQMI as a choropleth with method "auto"). Second layer: https://services.arcgis.com/P3ePLMYs2RVChkJx/arcgis/rest/services/Major_League_Baseball_Stadiums/FeatureServer/0 (colour by LEAGUE). Add a title slide, one feature slide for each state with two or more teams, and a closing "how this was built" slide. On each state slide show only the ballparks the state contains (slide layers with relation type "contains"); use transition "cut". Before writing the slides, query the ballparks service with each state's geometry and compare the result with each ballpark's STATE field; fix any mismatch and say how. Put it all in one map-v1 spec (https://gismap.online/schemas/map-v1.schema.json) and return the link and a QR code.

For an AI agent: check the relationship, then write the spec: The agent asked the ballparks service the same question each slide will ask, before relying on it. Ohio's generalized outline leaves Cincinnati's ballpark (on the Ohio River, the state line) in Kentucky, so the Ohio slide grows Ohio by 1 mile; growing Illinois the same way would wrongly pick up St. Louis's Busch Stadium across the Mississippi, so only Ohio is grown.

```js
import { mapSpec } from "https://gismap.online/js/gismap-core.js";

const STATES = "https://services.arcgis.com/P3ePLMYs2RVChkJx/arcgis/rest/services/USA_States_Generalized_Boundaries/FeatureServer/0";
const PARKS = "https://services.arcgis.com/P3ePLMYs2RVChkJx/arcgis/rest/services/Major_League_Baseball_Stadiums/FeatureServer/0";

// The same query a slide runs: which ballparks does this state contain?
async function ballparksIn(stateId, miles = 0) {
  const state = await (await fetch(`${STATES}/query?objectIds=${stateId}&returnGeometry=true&f=json`)).json();
  const body = new URLSearchParams({
    geometry: JSON.stringify(state.features[0].geometry), geometryType: "esriGeometryPolygon",
    inSR: JSON.stringify(state.spatialReference), spatialRel: "esriSpatialRelContains",
    outFields: "NAME,STATE", returnGeometry: "false", f: "json",
    ...(miles ? { distance: String(miles), units: "esriSRUnit_StatuteMile" } : {}),
  });
  const result = await (await fetch(`${PARKS}/query`, { method: "POST", body })).json();
  return result.features.map((feature) => feature.attributes.NAME);
}
await ballparksIn(36);    // Ohio: ["Progressive Field"], Cincinnati's park is missing
await ballparksIn(36, 1); // Ohio grown by 1 mile: both Ohio ballparks
await ballparksIn(14, 1); // Illinois grown by 1 mile: also Busch Stadium (Missouri), so don't

// Two layers, and slides that limit the ballparks per state (see map.json).
const spec = await (await fetch("https://gismap.online/examples/ai/mlb-ballparks-by-state/map.json")).json();
const { valid, issues } = mapSpec.validate(spec);
const { url, qr } = await mapSpec.createLink(spec); // compressed #map= link; qr: true when it fits a QR code
```

Caveats:

- Rogers Centre (Toronto Blue Jays) is in Canada, so no state slide shows it.
- Public data has small errors (this source spells Chase Field's city "Phoeniz"); check a field before quoting it on a slide.
- State outlines are generalized; spatial answers near rivers and coasts are worth checking, as above.
- Ballpark data last edited May 30, 2025.

### A styled map in one link, written by a chatbot

Chatbot. Any chatbot, even one that cannot run code, can make a styled county map by writing one JSON object into a link: corn sales by county, with "Not Disclosed" counties kept out of the colour classes.

Open it: https://gismap.online/#map=json:%7B%22version%22%3A1%2C%22basemap%22%3A%22gray-vector%22%2C%22layers%22%3A%5B%7B%22url%22%3A%22https%3A%2F%2Fservices.arcgis.com%2FP3ePLMYs2RVChkJx%2FArcGIS%2Frest%2Fservices%2FCorn%2FFeatureServer%2F0%22%2C%22renderer%22%3A%7B%22type%22%3A%22choropleth%22%2C%22field%22%3A%22CORN_SALES_IN_DOLLARS%22%2C%22method%22%3A%22auto%22%2C%22ramp%22%3A%22greens%22%2C%22exclude%22%3A%5B-1%5D%7D%7D%5D%7D

Page: https://gismap.online/examples/ai/corn-sales-one-link/

What it shows:

- A readable #map=json: link that a chat-only model can write by hand
- "exclude": [-1]: the publisher's "Not Disclosed" code is drawn as No data instead of distorting the classes
- "method": "auto": the app picks quantile classes because corn sales are heavily skewed

Prompt for a chatbot:

> Make a GIS Map Online link for U.S. corn sales by county. The layer is https://services.arcgis.com/P3ePLMYs2RVChkJx/ArcGIS/rest/services/Corn/FeatureServer/0; look at its fields with ?f=pjson and use CORN_SALES_IN_DOLLARS. Write a map-v1 spec (https://gismap.online/schemas/map-v1.schema.json) with a choropleth renderer, ramp "greens", method "auto" and a gray basemap. The publisher codes undisclosed counties as -1, so exclude -1. URI-encode the JSON and put it after https://gismap.online/#map=json: and give me the link.

For a code-running agent: An agent can find the -1 code itself instead of being told: sources.inspect reads the publisher's own style and reports it as a sentinel.

```js
import { sources, mapSpec } from "https://gismap.online/js/gismap-core.js";

const url = "https://services.arcgis.com/P3ePLMYs2RVChkJx/ArcGIS/rest/services/Corn/FeatureServer/0";
const meta = await sources.inspect(url);
const exclude = meta.sentinels.filter((code) => code.field === "CORN_SALES_IN_DOLLARS" && code.source !== "heuristic").map((code) => code.value); // [-1]
const spec = { version: 1, basemap: "gray-vector", layers: [{ url, renderer: { type: "choropleth", field: "CORN_SALES_IN_DOLLARS", method: "auto", ramp: "greens", exclude } }] };
const { valid } = mapSpec.validate(spec);
const { url: link } = await mapSpec.createLink(spec, { compress: false }); // the readable #map=json: form
```

Caveats:

- 546 of 3,074 counties are "Not Disclosed" (-1); they appear grey, as No data.
- Corn sales data last edited in August 2022.
- The layer hides itself when zoomed in past 1:144,447; add "ignoreServiceScaleRange": true to draw it at every zoom.

### A guided tour of eight classic ballparks

Guided tour. A guided tour that flies the 3D map from Fenway Park to Petco Park, with a caption at each of eight ballparks, opened from one link or QR code.

Tour link: https://gismap.online/?tourOnly=1#

Page: https://gismap.online/examples/tours/classic-ballparks/

Make it by hand:

1. Open Workflows, then Tours mode.
2. Fly to the first ballpark, tilt the view, and choose Add another chapter. Give the chapter a title and a short caption.
3. Repeat for each stop, then set the tour to play automatically.
4. Choose Share tour, and pick the tour-only link for a clean, full-screen tour.

Or generate it: Tours can be made from the features you already have, so the chapters come with their places filled in:

- From a briefing: add the Major League Baseball Stadiums layer, open Briefing, include the ballparks you want, choose Add included features as slides, then Make a guided tour from these slides. Each slide becomes a chapter at its feature; adjust each chapter's tilt and caption.
- From a field task: a task's Tour button turns its places and features into chapters.

For an AI agent: The tour link is base64url-encoded JSON after #tour=, so an agent can write it directly. Captions are kept to 80 characters, and the link must stay within 2,800 characters to fit a QR code.

```js
const tour = {
  v: 1, title: "Eight classic ballparks", skin: "clean-light", play: "auto",
  chapters: [
    { name: "Fenway Park", caption: "Boston Red Sox · opened 1912, the oldest ballpark in the majors",
      lat: 42.34622, lon: -71.09771, zoom: 16.6, tilt: 55, heading: 40, basemap: "satellite", linger: 6 },
    // … one object per stop (at most 50)
  ],
};
const base64url = (text) => btoa(String.fromCharCode(...new TextEncoder().encode(text))).replace(/\+/g, "-").replace(/\//g, "_").replace(/=+$/, "");
const link = `https://gismap.online/?tourOnly=1#tour=${base64url(JSON.stringify(tour))}`;
```

Caveats:

- A tour moves the camera only; it does not carry data layers. For data with slides, use a briefing.
- Add &autoplay=1 to the link to start playing as soon as it opens (not when the device asks for reduced motion).
- Ballpark coordinates come from the Major League Baseball Stadiums layer.

### A field task and its report, sent as two links

Field task. A two-ballpark field check sent as a link or QR code, and the completed report that comes back the same way: check-in, steps, features and notes, with no server.

Assignment link: https://gismap.online/?workflow=tasks#

Completed report (sample): https://gismap.online/?workflow=tasks#

Page: https://gismap.online/examples/field-tasks/opening-day-wayfinding/

Make it by hand:

1. Open Workflows, then Field tasks, and choose + New field task.
2. Write the title, instructions and steps. Choose Attach a feature from the map for each place to visit (up to five).
3. Choose Share to send the link or show its QR code.
4. The person in the field opens it, checks in, ticks off steps and places, writes a report and sends the link back. Opening that link shows the report.

Or generate it: Field tasks can come out of the work you have already done:

- From a briefing: an Actions slide's next steps become a field task with Send these as a field task.
- And back again: a task's Briefing and Tour buttons turn its features into a briefing or a tour.

Caveats:

- Everything is in the link, so anyone with it can read it: keep private details out of tasks and reports.
- A task holds up to 5 features, 10 steps and 500 characters of notes, so its link fits a QR code.
- The report here is a sample, written for this example; the app shows its times in your time zone.
